clue.text: Business arrangement is perfect, but one loses out

indicators.note: loses out says a letter drops out of the word for perfect

parts.note: perfect means ideal
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A trader complains that a seemingly perfect business arrangement leaves one party worse off.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal is an agreement between parties, typically commercial, so a business arrangement fits as a synonym.

clue.text: Gruff ace grabbed by hack maybe

indicators.note: grabbed by says the ace letter is held inside the animal word

parts.note: a hack is a riding horse, hence the 'maybe' signalling an example
A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A gruff journalist, an ace reporter perhaps, is snapped up by a tabloid hack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' reads as a journalist, but here it is a horse kept for ordinary riding.
explanation.definitionFit: A gruff voice is rough and husky, a close synonym of a croaky throat.

clue.text: Hands going up for mutually acceptable 1 Down

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: paws is a jocular word for hands

explanation.surface: Hands are raised to signal agreement to a mutually acceptable business deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 Down is DEAL, so the definition is a mutually acceptable deal.
explanation.definitionFit: An exchange both parties accept is a trade, an even-handed transaction of one thing for another.

clue.text: Flexible article wedged into short block at base

indicators.note: wedged into says the article is pushed inside the shortened block word
short means the last letter is cut off the block word

parts.note: a plinth is the block at the base of a column or statue
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A flexible item is jammed into a short block at the base, like a shim.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pliant bends easily, a synonym of supple or yielding.

clue.text: Rustic not losing heart, but tricky to teach

indicators.note: tricky suggests the letters are arranged in an awkward new order
losing heart means the middle letter of the word not is removed

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin who keeps his nerve is nonetheless hard to teach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' leaves NT from 'not'; 'tricky' rearranges RUSTIC with NT.
explanation.definitionFit: To instruct is to teach or train someone, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Attlee elected, source of embarrassment for his rival's wife

parts.note: Clement Attlee was the British Labour prime minister of 1945
elected means in, as a party voted into office

indicators.note: source of means just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Attlee's 1945 election win embarrassed his defeated rival Churchill and his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Attlee beat Winston Churchill in the 1945 UK general election; Churchill's wife was Clementine.
explanation.definitionFit: Clementine Churchill was married to Winston Churchill, Attlee's political opponent.

clue.text: Were nine players coming back to present cutting-edge piece?

indicators.note: coming back says the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: were and was are both past forms of to be
a nonet is a group of nine musicians

explanation.surface: A question about whether nine musicians returned to perform an avant-garde composition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting-edge piece' sounds like modern music; it is a saw, a tool with a cutting edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodworking tool with a toothed blade is a piece of equipment literally having a cutting edge.

clue.text: Attack puts one out

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: An attack in sport, say cricket, puts one batsman out.
explanation.definitionFit: To be set upon is to be assaulted, so the phrasal verb means attack.

clue.text: See any number going to cathedral location wanting company?

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
N stands for an unspecified number in maths
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A visitor heading to a cathedral city wonders whether they are craving companionship.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lonely is isolated and longs for companions, a clear synonym.

clue.text: St Francis's friend first to taste wine

parts.note: St Clare of Assisi was a follower and friend of St Francis

indicators.note: first to means the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A saint's companion is first to sample the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine.

clue.text: Ghosts in quiet county enthralling old maiden

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the county holds the other letters

parts.note: Hants is the abbreviation for Hampshire, an English county
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Spooks in a sleepy shire captivate an elderly unmarried woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Phantoms are apparitions or spectres, synonyms of spirits of the dead.

clue.text: Sort of manoeuvre requiring time — Ruth struggling with tin-opener

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters are wrestled into a different order

explanation.surface: Ruth takes her time wrestling with a can opener.
explanation.definitionFit: A driving move turning a car round in a narrow road using forward, reverse, forward.

clue.text: This person in Euston, say, follows the chap shilly-shallying

indicators.note: follows places the station part after the pronoun

parts.note: he is the pronoun for the chap

indicators.note: in puts the first-person letter inside the railway word

parts.note: Euston is a London railway station, an example
this person, the speaker, is I

explanation.surface: Someone at Euston dithers behind another man.
explanation.definitionFit: Shilly-shallying is indecisive wavering, a synonym of dithering pause.

clue.text: Jeremy's items in golf bag?

definitions.meaning: the surname of the actor Jeremy, star of Brideshead Revisited

explanation.surface: A question about what a famous actor called Jeremy keeps in his golf bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf clubs with metal heads are named for the metal; Jeremy Irons is an English actor.

clue.text: Wine that's nastier putting some characters off

indicators.note: putting some characters off says several letters are removed from the word nastier

explanation.surface: A wine that tastes so nasty it puts some people off.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing N, E and R from NASTIER leaves the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white wine from Piedmont in Italy.

clue.text: Home I abandon, the ultimate in cruelty and wickedness

parts.note: in means at home
to quit is to abandon

indicators.note: the ultimate in means the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A tale of leaving home and the height of cruelty and wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Iniquity is gross injustice or sin, a synonym of evil conduct.

clue.text: Stony woman from province given birthday honour?

parts.note: NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province
an OBE is a British honour often awarded in the monarch's Birthday Honours list

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted woman from Ulster receives a royal award.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth this mother, weeping for her slain children, was turned to stone.
explanation.definitionFit: The mythical Theban queen became a rock, so she is literally a woman of stone.

clue.text: Cain — he'd turned into a beast

indicators.note: turned into suggests the letters are changed into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: The murderer Cain transformed into a monster.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiny anteater of Australia is an animal, so beast fits generally.

clue.text: Holiday providing 'adult entertainment' — keep son away!

indicators.note: keep away says the son letter is excluded from the word

parts.note: a strip show is adult entertainment

explanation.surface: A parent wants a holiday with racy shows but without the boy along.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is a short journey or excursion, a synonym of a break away.

clue.text: Like close pals unintelligent in respect of wrongdoing?

definitions.meaning: read literally: as stupid as criminals

explanation.surface: Description of friends who are close yet dim about crime.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means very friendly; read literally it says dense like robbers.

clue.text: Young animal in trap set up under equipment

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the trap word below the equipment

parts.note: kit means equipment

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: a net is a trap

explanation.surface: A baby creature caught in a snare is placed beneath some gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A young cat is the classic example of a juvenile animal.

clue.text: Royal personage? Journalist must take care

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist
a ward is a person in someone's care, or the care itself

explanation.surface: A reporter must be careful around a royal figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Several English kings bore the name, so it identifies a royal person by example.

clue.text: Peacock to make spasmodic sounds blocking entrance to rockery

indicators.note: blocking means sitting inside, so a letter is put within the speech word

parts.note: to stutter is to speak in spasms

indicators.note: entrance to means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A peacock squawks jerkily while barring the way into a rock garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A strutter is a vain show-off, figuratively a peacock.

clue.text: Stay to offer support

definitions.meaning: a prop, as in an armrest

explanation.surface: An instruction to remain on hand to help.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means remain or linger; as a noun it is a prop holding something up, like a cue rest in snooker.

clue.text: Move slowly in fringes of wood within valley

indicators.note: within puts the edge letters inside the valley word

parts.note: a dale is a valley

indicators.note: fringes of means the first and last letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Ambling along the edges of a wood in a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: To dawdle is to linger or amble, a synonym of dallying.

clue.text: Chance bottle won't open

indicators.note: won't open means the first letter is lost

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or pluck

explanation.surface: There is a chance the bottle will not open.
explanation.definitionFit: Luck is fortune or chance, a near synonym.

clue.text: Tree trunk in which is found dry container

indicators.note: in which is found says the dry letters sit inside the trunk word

parts.note: a bole is the trunk of a tree
TT means teetotal, dry

explanation.surface: A hollow tree trunk holds a parched vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottle is a vessel for liquids, a kind of container.

clue.text: Phoney 'diamond' produced by plant

parts.note: sham means fake or phoney
rock is slang for a diamond

explanation.surface: A fake diamond turned out by a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' reads as a factory but is the clover-like Irish emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: Shamrock is a small clover, the national plant emblem of Ireland.
